links.outcome: Physician task load (PTL) and burnout in intervention vs control clinicians
links.effect: PTL was lower in the intervention arm (−27.4; 95% CI −49.4 to −5.3; P=0.02) and burnout was lower (−0.20); charting time showed no significant difference (−1.2 seconds).
links.quote: The adjusted between-arm difference in PTL at follow-up favored the intervention arm (scale 0-400; −27.4; 95% CI, −49.4 to −5.3; P=0.02).

links.outcome: Clinician usability and acceptance (net promoter score) and sustained use of the tool
links.effect: Net promoter score was −22. Summaries interacted with fell from 21.5% to 10.5%, and monthly clinician use fell from 88.7% to 66.2%.
links.quote: The net promoter score was −22, indicating that on average, clinicians did not recommend the tool.

screen.reason: This is a pragmatic randomized controlled trial evaluating the deployment of Epic's EHR-integrated generative AI chart summarization tool versus usual care on clinician task load, burnout, and usage in real-world clinical practice.
